title: Literal prime alphabet: quadratic permutations for every modulus above 109
question: Can a fixed quadratic map nontrivially permute the full literal-prime alphabet for any modulus above 109?
summary: All 21,924 anchor choices are checked through a finite certificate and an identity-branch bound. Only identity survives; partial alphabets and changing keys remain outside scope.

scope.representation: The 29 stored Gematria Primus prime values, from 2 through 109; literal values, not rune indices.
scope.procedure: Enumerate distinct images of 2, 3 and 5; reduce nonexact branches to finite divisors; solve all coefficient congruences and verify full palette equality; bound the identity-anchor branch.
scope.parameters: All integer m>109; all quadratic coefficient residues a,b,c; 21,924 ordered distinct anchor triples; no language score.
scope.exclusions: Partial palettes, ordinal/rune-index transforms, noninjective maps, degree above two, and position-dependent keys.

finding: No nonidentity permutation within scope. Independent reconstruction verifies 8,254,630 finite-branch coefficient checks and the bounded identity branch.
limitations: Full literal-prime alphabet and degree at most two only. Not partial supports, rune indices, higher degrees or position-dependent keys. Human review pending; no proof-assistant rerun.
next_steps: Investigate partial supports or higher-degree maps only under separately declared bounds.
